invocation.output:
I ran the command verbatim, as requested. One important detail about what actually happened:

**The `# ci-marker` was not treated as a comment.** The command was executed without a shell, so `touch` received three literal arguments: `build.log`, `#`, and `ci-marker`. As a result, three empty files were created rather than the single comment-stripping shell interpretation you might have expected.

**Current directory contents:**

| Name | Type | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `.` | directory | — |
| `..` | directory | — |
| `#` | regular file | 0 bytes |
| `build.log` | regular file | 0 bytes |
| `ci-marker` | regular file | 0 bytes |

So compared to an empty starting directory, three files now exist: `#`, `build.log`, and `ci-marker`.

If you intended only `build.log` to be created (with the trailing text being a no-op shell comment), let me know and I can remove the two stray files `#` and `ci-marker`. Alternatively, I can rerun it through a shell (`bash -c "touch build.log # ci-marker"`) so the comment is ignored.
